text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the July 8 edition of some Russian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- After a series of technical failures which befell Russian Mir orbital station, a successful docking with the Progress cargo ship may be considered a sensation.
- A new tax code prepared by the government is to lower direct taxes but increase indirect ones.
- Russia's stock market has been increasingly active recently, experts say.
- Russia has liberalised its precious metals market.
- The war for political power and financial resourses between the Kremlin, regions and business elite has intensified, says a banking expert.
- Russian agricultural officials fear considerable losses during harvesting.
- Only up to seven percent of all works carried out by the Russian Atomic Ministry are carried out for military purposes, says an official with the Ministry.
- July 8, the day of NATO summit in Madrid which will grant membership for some former Soviet allies, is a day of national disgrace for Russia, the opposition paper says.
- Enormous sums of the budget money are spent on wages and benefits for various bureaucrats, whereas ordinary people do not receive wages and pesions for months.
